hook_text: One farmhouse in the Karoo. Ten homesteads on a hill. A fishing village with a church and a shop. Which is which?
clip_script: A settlement is anywhere people live. Out in the countryside, settlements are small. An isolated farmstead is one farmhouse on its own, kilometres from the next. A hamlet is a little cluster of homes with almost no services. A village is bigger, with a school, a shop, a church, maybe a clinic. People settled where there was water, flat land and good soil. And they stayed because of the work: maize and sheep, coal and platinum, pine plantations, and on the West Coast, rock lobster and snoek. Houses far apart: dispersed. Houses close together: nucleated. Read the dots on the map, and you can read the land.
visual_style: A whiteboard landscape drawn from above: one lone farmhouse, a small cluster of huts, then a village around a church, with icons for farming, mining, forestry and fishing.
pacing: Calm build up the hierarchy, quicker through the four activities.
